ops.title: When extending a subsystem to a second backend, design a first-class interface, not parallel per-backend package functions
ops.body:
Reviewing a cc-pool plan that added `DeleteFileCredential()` + a standalone `Headless()` probe as loose keychain-package functions, the user said: "this seems a bit hacky, we should figure out the right first-class credentials interface here."

**Why:** Bolt-on per-backend functions (Read/ReadFile/Write/WriteFile...) keep backends as parallel special cases every caller must know about; a small per-location interface (e.g. `creds.Store`) plus first-class error values (e.g. `ErrUnavailable` for a headless keychain) makes every caller correct by construction.

**How to apply:** When a plan or change grows a second storage/transport/provider variant, stop and design the small interface each variant implements — including expressing environmental failure modes as sentinel errors on the interface, not side-channel probes. This complements [[prefers-minimal-fixes-no-guard-layers]]: minimal means no defensive layers, not skipping the right abstraction.
